publisher: GEBCO (General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans) / Seabed 2030, hosted as a public COG mirror by source.coop (user alexgleith)
obtained_via: HTTP range-request (vsicurl) windowed read of the global COG, no full download, no auth/key required
method: python3 + rasterio, rasterio.windows.from_bounds against /vsicurl/<url>, read band 1 only within bbox, wrote a new small GeoTIFF (no reprojection)
approx_resolution_m: ~450 m at this latitude (15 arc-second native grid)
units: metres, negative = below sea level (bathymetry), positive = elevation (topography) — standard GEBCO convention, NOT chart datum/soundings datum
licence: GEBCO Grid: released under a public-domain-equivalent / CC0-style GEBCO terms — free for any use with acknowledgement of GEBCO/Seabed2030 as source (see https://www.gebco.net/about_us/faq/). Verify exact wording before redistribution; the source.coop mirror inherits the same terms.
notes: Coarse global compilation, NOT a hydrographic survey — do not use for navigation.
Vertical datum is approximate mean sea level, not NZ chart datum (LAT) — do not mix directly with LINZ tide/drying-height data without a datum note.

Good only as a rough shelf/basin-scale sanity check or a placeholder deep-water gradient outside the harbour mouth; at ~450 m/pixel it cannot resolve the harbour's channels, sandbars or the ebb-tide delta (those are ~50-500 m features) — this is the fallback baseline referenced in ROADMAP.md J6, not the deliverable.
